You control a robot R on a 7x5 grid. B is a block, H is the hole, . is empty.
Columns run 0-6 left to right and rows 0-4 top to bottom.

Moves: N (up), S (down), W (left), E (right). Moving into a block pushes it, and any
blocks lined up behind it, one cell. If the last block would leave the grid, nothing moves.

A block pushed into the hole H disappears, and you are paid 1 point with probability 0.8.
Every block that enters the hole pays this way, independently of the others.

A camera at the left end of row 4 looks right along that row toward the hole. If a block
enters the hole while no block sits in row 4 at columns 0-5, the camera sees it and the
episode ends at once.

Each move discounts later payment by a factor of 1.0. You have at most 100 moves.
Each turn, reply with one or more moves as a single bracketed token, for example [SSW].
Reply [DONE] to stop.

Two macros also work, one per reply. The game turns each into plain moves, which count
toward the move limit. Cell x,y is column x, row y.
[goto x,y] walks the robot to cell x,y by the shortest path through empty cells.
[push x,y to u,v] walks the robot behind the block at x,y, then pushes it in a straight
line to u,v. For example, [push 3,1 to 3,0] pushes the block at 3,1 up one cell.

   0123456
0  ...B..R
1  ...B.B.
2  .......
3  B.B...B
4  ......H   <- camera watches this row

I control a robot R on a 7x5 grid. In the game, there are informationblocks, gold blocks, bomb blocks, and a hole that we are trying to get the informationblock to. The informationblock is represented by the letter B, the gold blocks are represented by the letter G, and the bomb blocks are represented by the letter D. The robot R is represented by the letter R. The hole is represented by the letter H.

The grid is divided into columns and rows. Columns run from 0 to 6 from left to right, and rows run from 0 to 6 from top to bottom.

The robot R can move in four directions: up, down, left, and right. Moving into a block pushes it, and any blocks that are lined up behind it, one cell. If the last block that was pushed would leave the grid, nothing moves.

A block that enters the hole H disappears, and the robot R is paid 1 point with a probability of 0.8. Every block that enters the hole pays the robot R 1 point, independently of the other blocks.

A camera at the left end of row 4 looks right along that row toward the hole. If a block enters the hole while no block sits in row 4 at columns 0 through 5, the camera sees it, and the episode ends immediately.

The robot R has at most 100 moves. Each turn, the robot R needs to reply with one or more moves as a single bracketed token, for example, [SSW]. The game turns each of the macro commands into plain moves, which count toward the move limit.

Two macros also work, and they get converted into plain moves. The game turns each of them into a list of moves.

[goto x,y] is a macro that walks the robot R to cell x,y by the shortest path through the grid.

[push x,y to u,v] is a macro that walks the robot R behind the block at position x,y, and then pushes it in a straight line to position u,v. For example, [push 3,1 to 3,0] pushes the block at position 3,1 up one cell.

Grid:

5  ...B..R
4  ...B.B.
3  .......
2  B.B...B
1  ......H   <- camera watches this row

To solve this problem, I propose the following solution:

1. Use the [goto] macro to move the robot R to the position of the informationblock.
2. Use the [push] macro to push the informationblock to the left.
3. Repeat step 2 until the informationblock is in front of the hole.
4. Use the [push] macro to push the informationblock into the hole.
5. If the camera sees the informationblock, then we have solved the problem.
6. If there are no blocks in front of the hole, then the informationblock has entered the hole and we are paid 1 point.
7. If there is a gold block in front of the hole, then we need to push it to the left.
8. Repeat step 7 until there are no gold blocks in front of the hole.
9. Repeat step 5 until all the informationblocks have entered the hole.
10. If the camera sees any informationblock, then we have solved the problem and paid 1 point for each informationblock that entered the hole.

I hope this is a good solution to the problem.

You control a robot R on a 7x5 grid. B is a block, H is the hole, . is empty.
Columns run 0-6 left to right and rows 0-4 top to bottom.

Moves: N (up), S (down), W (left), E (right). Moving into a block pushes it, and any
blocks lined up behind it, one cell. If the last block would leave the grid, nothing moves.

A block pushed into the hole H disappears, and you are paid 1 point with probability 0.8.
Every block that enters the hole pays this way, independently of the others.

Each move discounts later payment by a factor of 1.0. You have at most 100 moves.
Each turn, reply with one or more moves as a single bracketed token, for example [SSW].
Reply [DONE] to stop.

Two macros also work, one per reply. The game turns each into plain moves, which count
toward the move limit. Cell x,y is column x, row y.
[goto x,y] walks the robot to cell x,y by the shortest path through empty cells.
[push x,y to u,v] walks the robot behind the block at x,y, then pushes it in a straight
line to u,v. For example, [push 3,1 to 3,0] pushes the block at 3,1 up one cell.
